title: Homogeneous quotient action on an arbitrary degree kernel
statement: Let j:Z→X be a closed immersion, J=ker j with J²=0, and L an invertible module. Let T be a TensorGradedPresentation j L with ideal I, maps k_d, b_d and c_d [lem-sc-square-zero-tensor-graded-presentation]. For a,d,t≥0, h:d+a=t, and s:O_Z→j*(L^a), define m:J_d→J_t on Z, with J_r=j*(J tensor L^r), by the explicit composite tensorIdealSectionMultiply: the inverse right unitor, J_d tensor s, the inverse boundaryPullbackTensorIso, then pullback of the associator, tensor-power multiplication and the degree transport h [lem-sc-square-zero-ideal-tensor-unit]. Define v:K_d→K_t by boundaryIdealKernelIso_d inverse, the unit on J tensor L^d, j_*(m), the inverse unit on J tensor L^t and boundaryIdealKernelIso_t, where K_r=ker eta_(L^r). Let sigma_U:C(U)→End(I(U)) and mu:C(X)→End(I) be ring maps satisfying i(sigma_U(p(b))y)=b i(y) and (mu(g))_U(y)=sigma_U(g restricted to U)y. Then k_d ≫ mu(c_a(s(1)))=v ≫ k_t. There is no block degree n, coefficient comparison D or cohomology assertion.

proof.text: Apply closedImmersion_unit_epi to L^a and transport its adjunction to the canonical one by unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app. Mathlib isLocallySurjective_iff_epi gives local lifts of s(1) on a covering of each open. The b_quotient equation and naturality of c identify p(b_a(x)) with the restriction of the one global quotient coefficient.

Use k_inclusion at the source, hglobal, and hlocal to compute the included action as b_a(x) times b_d(inclusion y). Commute the factors in B and apply b_multiply in degrees d and a. The local ideal-tensor formula computes the inclusion of tensorHomogeneousKernelMap(y) as the tensorPowAddIso product of inclusion y with x. Apply k_inclusion at the target and eliminate the degree transport h by equality induction; the two included sections agree. Cancel the monic i, provided by T.shortExact.

Use naturality of both global module maps to identify their restrictions with the local calculation. Apply TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq on the local lifting cover to obtain equality on every open, then module-map extensionality. No global lift or arbitrary quotient-section restriction law is required. The same proof handles zero degrees and empty opens.

theorem tensorHomogeneousKernel_action {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (j : Z ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion j] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hI : j.ker ^ 2 = ⊥)
    (T : TensorGradedPresentation j L) (a d t : ℕ) (h : d + a = t)
    (s : 𝟙_ Z.Modules ⟶ (tensorPullback j).obj (L.tensorPow a))
    (σ : ∀ U : X.Opens, T.C.right.obj.obj (op U) →+*
      Module.End ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).obj.obj (op U)) (T.I.val.obj (op U)))
    (μ : T.C.right.obj.obj (op ⊤) →+* End T.I)
    (hlocal : ∀ (U : X.Opens) (b : T.B.right.obj.obj (op U)) (y : T.I.val.obj (op U)),
      @id (T.B.right.obj.obj (op U))
        (T.i.val.app (op U) (σ U (T.p.right.hom.app (op U) b) y)) =
        b * @id (T.B.right.obj.obj (op U)) (T.i.val.app (op U) y))
    (hglobal : ∀ (g : T.C.right.obj.obj (op ⊤)) (U : X.Opens)
      (y : T.I.val.obj (op U)),
      (μ g).val.app (op U) y = σ U (T.C.right.obj.map (homOfLE le_top).op g) y) :
    T.k d ≫ μ ((T.c a).app ⊤ (s.app ⊤ (1 : Γ(Z, ⊤)))) =
      tensorHomogeneousKernelMap j L hI a d t h s ≫ T.k t
